summary: Ported CSS-injection logic from the registry's web-extension builder into the gizmo repo's build script so emitted CSS assets get installed via a keyed <style> tag instead of being dropped silently. Added a regression test, fixed two bugs (wrong variable name `entries`, treating bundles as entries), and verified with vitest (3/3) and svelte-check (0 errors). Then committed the gizmo changes plus the prior transport refactor in two separate commits.
decisions: Web-extension builder now flattens bundle outputs into a single `entries` array and both chunk-selection and CSS collection iterate over it, matching the registry builder's structure.
CSS injection uses a <style> tag keyed by `package`-derived styleKey with a `data-gizmo-extension-style` attribute so reinstalls replace cleanly.
Regression test fixture uses a plain `.css` import from the entry, with lenient assertions on `fixture-panel`, `color:red`, and `data-gizmo-extension-style` rather than tying to exact formatting.
Split into two commits: (1) transport refactor owning agent resources by the server, (2) narrow-width sidebar fixes + web-extension CSS-injection, so each commit is a coherent unit.
errors: Initial port referenced `entries.flatMap(...)` but the gizmo code defined `outputs`/`chunks` only — caused ReferenceError on the CSS collection path.

First CSS test failed with empty CSS because the code iterated `outputs` (bundles) instead of flattening to per-entry assets; fixed by introducing `entries = outputs.flatMap(...)` and iterating `entries`.
